title: Who Should Lead Nvidia Next?
text:
Daniel Nenni
Founder
Staff member

Please continue to add to the collection of quotes.

Advice to the Nvidia Board of Directors:

“If you don't bring Jensen back, I would not hire an outsider. Nvidia is too complicated.” Jeff Bezos. Bezos made the remarks at a Semafor conference on November 17. He said outside CEOs have a “vanishingly small chance of succeeding” and called hiring one a “last resort.” Bezos had years to plan his own handoff to Andy Jassy at Amazon. NVIDIA is conducting a search after Huang’s abrupt departure, with CFO Colette Kress serving as interim CEO. The board says it will consider both internal and external candidates.

U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent gave the clearest alternative to Bezos’s advice. He urged NVIDIA to look outside the company for its next CEO, saying on Fox News, “They need a dramatic shake-up.”

- Elon Musk, Replit CEO Amjad Masad, and Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan backed the campaign to reinstate Jensen Huang.

- President Donald Trump signaled support for Huang’s return. Asked about reinstating him, Trump said, “I would not mind that.” washingtonpost.com

- Investor Armina Rosenberg, whose firm owns NVIDIA shares, spelled out what investors want from the board: “a named CEO, answers on the regulatory questions and signs the engineering team is staying.”

- "Jensen is one of the great builders of our time. We cannot starve the future of his innovation and industrial breakthroughs," reads a comment from Uber cofounder Travis Kalanick on Stand With Jensen, an online petition with more than 186,000 signatures. "To err is human," Kalanick who said he is crowdsourcing "wild ideas" to get Huang reinstated — added.

Tatiana Koffman, a GP at Moonwalker Capital, said Nvidia's board should finish its investigation, and that Huang should be reinstated if it finds no credible proof of a security breach.

- " I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO" Jensen Huang former Nvidia CEO.

- NVIDIA board chair Harvey Jones said on November 17 that the board does not intend to reinstate Huang. The permanent search remains open to both internal and external candidates.
